title: The residue reduction controls integral Tor amplitude
statement:
Fix the global finite-field coefficient datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi=\varpi_E$, and a scheme $X$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Put $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\geq1$ and $\kappa=A_1$. Let $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ in the derived-complete integral sense of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and write $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\widehat R_X}(A_n)_X$ for its derived reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. For integers $a\leq b$, if $K_1$ has cohomology only in $[a,b]$, then every $K_n$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Consequently
$$D^b_c(X,R)=D^b_{ctf}(X,R)$$
with $D^b_{ctf}$ defined by the uniform finite-level Tor condition of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. This assertion does not equate constructibility with site-perfectness on the whole scheme.

proof.text: For a finite reduction choose a cochain representative L and its isomorphism e to the derived reduction, using essential surjectivity of Q. Resolve L by a K-flat P. Integral constructibility supplies finite-level constructibility; the closed-under-isomorphisms clause of the bounded-constructible theorem transports it to Q(L).

source.place: Proof; K-flat realization of coefficient tensor associativity

proof.text: Apply the pro-etale residue Tor test to L with its resolution P. The residue homology comparison identifies zero cohomology of the residue tensor with zero cohomology of the level-one reduction. Outside [a,b], the latter follows by contradiction from the support hypothesis. Transport the resulting amplitude from Q(L) to the reduction by composing representative isomorphisms in its universal K-flat test.

proof.text: The common cohomology interval in integral constructibility bounds the first reduction. Apply the preceding finite-level argument with this interval for every n. This gives integral finite-Tor membership. The reverse implication is the first conjunct of that membership predicate; function extensionality and propositional extensionality prove equality.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ in the actual sense of
[def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. If $K_1$ has
cohomology in $[a,b]$, then every $K_n$ has Tor amplitude
in $[a,b]$. Consequently

$$
D^b_c(X,R)=D^b_{ctf}(X,R)
$$

for this DVR coefficient category. This does not equate
constructibility with site-perfectness on the whole scheme.

proof.text:
Associativity of coefficient tensor product gives
$K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}\kappa=K_1$.
Each $K_n$ is bounded constructible by
[def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. The residue Tor test
[lem-exc-residue-tor-test], applied to the local Artinian
ring $A_n$, therefore gives the same Tor interval $[a,b]$
at every $n$. This is precisely the integral condition in
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. The reverse inclusion is
part of that definition.
